bottom_line: All three auctions are scanned with every photo viewed, and each has a market pass showing sold prices, unsold results and asking prices separately. Only sold prices set a maximum bid. The most solid evidence: 1964 Macallan (lot 768), Ebatarinja watercolour (lot 62), Perth Mint Federation gold and silver coin (lot 876), Cardhu 2020 (lot 677), Tiffany bangle (lot 849) and, if the signature proves genuine, the Haughton Forrest oil (lot 1016). Many lots are already bid at or past their ceilings, and the cards say so. Wine has almost no sold data. Catalogues 4 and 5 exist but have not been scanned. Bids move fast near the close, so check them before you act. Your browser comps are added under "Added from your browser comps" on each lot: most came back as asking prices or category guides, so few maximum bids changed. Two things to note: the gold coin (lot 876) has a melt value of about A$1,700 for its gold centre alone against a $700 bid, and the cautious KEEP ceiling for the Macallan (lot 768) is nearer $3,175 after the lower Whisky Hunter results.
